angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 131,487 km at 14.88 pc = 0.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 67.2123 +/- 0.0187 mas (same row, RUWE 1.16): 14.88 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.189 +/- 0.006 solar radii from Nagel et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of LHS 3844 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...710A.311N/abstract): 131,487 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.151 +/- 0.014 solar masses from Nagel et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of LHS 3844 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...710A.311N/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3080 +/- 50 K from Nagel et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 3844 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...710A.311N/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Nagel et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 3844 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...710A.311N/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/lhs-3844.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.064, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 3844 (pscomppars): spectral type M4.5-M5.0, from Nagel et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...710A.311N/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 3844 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.22 dex, from Nagel et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...710A.311N/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 3844 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -2.56543, from Nagel et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...710A.311N/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 3844 (pscomppars): age 7.8 Gyr, from Nagel et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...710A.311N/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 3844 (pscomppars): rotation period 130 d, from Nagel et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...710A.311N/abstract)
